channel.title: Fly Kai Tak blog
channel.description: News and features from Fly Kai Tak, a browser flight simulator of the 1998 Runway 13 approach into Hong Kong Kai Tak.

item.title: Boats along the seawall, not in the inlet
item.description: Boats pass right alongside Kai Tak's runway seawall again, as in the 1990s, but never enter the inlet under the taxiways to the south apron.

item.title: Wider spacing between taxiing aircraft
item.description: Taxiing aircraft at Kai Tak now keep double the gap on the taxiways. Departures queuing at the runway end can still close up.

item.title: The checkerboard turn tightens at the end
item.description: Kai Tak's checkerboard turn now starts gently and tightens to about 25° of bank over Kowloon City before rolling out on the runway.

item.title: Maintenance apron now matches the flight apron
item.description: The Kai Tak maintenance apron in front of the hangars now uses the same concrete colour as the main flight apron, with no dark patch or seam.

item.title: The checkerboard turn now starts at 650 ft, 2 NM out
item.description: Kai Tak's checkerboard turn now starts about 2 NM out at 650 ft and rolls out near 140 ft, with an orange-and-white checkerboard.

item.title: One bridge, a joined-up apron and a wider taxiway
item.description: Kai Tak's apron now runs into the south apron, one bridge crosses the inlet, and the taxiway tarmac widens near the Runway 31 end.

item.title: The control tower is back on the terminal roof
item.description: The Kai Tak control tower moves to its real spot on the terminal roof at the runway end, rebuilt from period photos with outward-leaning glass.

item.title: Follow Fly Kai Tak on Facebook and Instagram
item.description: Follow Fly Kai Tak on Facebook and Instagram at @flykaitak. Both are now linked from the home screen and every blog page.

item.title: Harbour shipping follows the fairways
item.description: Moving ships follow the Marine Department fairways and traffic separation schemes, one way and keeping right, while most harbour vessels lie moored or at anchor.

item.title: Separate menus for flight, spotter and terminal views
item.description: Kai Tak's camera menu is now three: Flight views, Plane spotter spots and a new Terminal interior menu for the hall, immigration, arcade, gate lounge, stairs and entrance.

item.title: South apron, helipads and inlet taxiways
item.description: Kai Tak's south apron with stands 71-81, helipads and taxiway bridges over the inlet, plus fuel tanks beside the terminal and bitumen at the maintenance hangars.

item.title: Inside the 1998 terminal: staff and signs
item.description: The Kai Tak terminal now has a 1998 interior: check-in desks, departure immigration, a shop arcade, arrivals, signs and staff including armed security.

item.title: Maintenance area moved to the chart position
item.description: The Kai Tak maintenance area is repositioned to match the 1996 parking chart and airport plan: hangars, workshop tower, compound and offices turned to the chart angle.

item.title: Maintenance area: hangars and tank farm
item.description: Kai Tak's maintenance area now has three hangars with lit bays, a workshop tower, a fenced aircraft compound, a blast fence, floodlights and a fuel tank farm.

item.title: Remote stands and apron buses
item.description: Remote stands 11 to 19 at Kai Tak hold parked aircraft, and apron buses run from a new bus gate to their doors when no jet bridge is free.

item.title: Cargo terminal and freighters
item.description: Kai Tak gets a cargo terminal with stands 41 to 46, 747-400F and A300-600F freighters in the schedule, cargo loaders and trucks, plus new hangars and car park detail.

item.title: Real Housing Authority estates
item.description: Public housing estates now use the Housing Authority's estate list: the 101 estates from 1998 inside the map, each rebuilt from its real block types and heights.

item.title: Public housing estates in bunches
item.description: Hong Kong public housing blocks (Harmony, Trident, Twin Tower and slab) now stand in matching estates in the sim, with pastel facades, air-conditioners and roof tanks.

item.title: Share buttons on the home screen
item.description: The home screen now has share buttons for X, Facebook, Reddit, WhatsApp, Threads, email, copy link and the system share sheet, in English or Cantonese.

item.title: Bay lines on the car park roof
item.description: The Plane Spotter car park roof now has white parking bay lines: a row against the far wall and three double rows with aisles between them.

item.title: More detail on the car park roof
item.description: The Plane Spotter car park roof now has globe lamps, a pipe railing and crowd barrier, a painted deck and a stairwell entry with exit and caution signs.

item.title: FAA signs and markings on the airfield
item.description: Fly Kai Tak now has FAA-style airfield signs and markings: touchdown-zone bars, hold lines, link taxiways B1 to B6, and mandatory, location, direction and distance signs.

item.title: Fix: Aircraft Stay on the Tarmac
item.description: Fly Kai Tak ground fix: arrivals leave the runway by a link taxiway, every aircraft keeps its wheels on the tarmac, and the grass is off limits.

item.title: The map is off until you turn it on
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's corner map now starts hidden on the home screen and in flights. Press M or tick Map with live aircraft under Options to show it.

item.title: A longer thrust bar for finer control
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's thrust lever bar is now up to 260 px tall on desktop and 170 px on landscape phones, giving finer control of thrust.

item.title: A bigger map on the home screen and in Plane Spotter
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's corner map is now double size on the home screen and in Plane Spotter, and the home screen map moves clear of the High scores panel.

item.title: Flight Board Key and Button
item.description: Switch the Fly Kai Tak flight information board on and off with the B key on the home screen as well as in Plane Spotter, or with the new Flights button.

item.title: New: link taxiways between the runway and taxiway A
item.description: Fly Kai Tak update: five angled bitumen link taxiways now join the runway to parallel taxiway A, matching the aerial photographs of Kai Tak.

item.title: Rooftop Cross-Bar Lights on the Approach
item.description: Three bright cross-bar lamp masts on tall Kowloon rooftops now mark the approach to Runway 13 and Runway 31, glowing at night under the flight path.

item.title: Update: starter scores on the high score table
item.description: Fly Kai Tak update: the high score table now starts with ten fictional, easy-to-beat scores, from 58 down to 15.

item.title: Concorde at Kai Tak: The Rare Visits
item.description: Concorde's rare visits to Kai Tak: the 1976 sales tour, a 1985 charter, and how Fly Kai Tak's Concorde special lands, taxis and takes off.

item.title: A Concorde Visits Kai Tak
item.description: Plane Spotter gets a rare Concorde-style special: a drooped-nose delta-wing jet that lands hourly, parks at stand 6 and leaves, with its own gold board rows.

item.title: The map on the home screen, with M to toggle
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's corner map now shows automatically on the home screen over the live demo flight, and the M key toggles it on and off, on the home screen and in flight.

item.title: New: a landing lesson for first-time pilots
item.description: Fly Kai Tak now has a Landing lesson: a coach panel walks first-time pilots through the Runway 13 IGS approach in nine steps with live meters and plain-language tips.

item.title: A Map option on the home screen
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's home screen now has a Map with live aircraft option, so you can start a flight with the corner map on or off. M still toggles it in flight.

item.title: A map toggle with live aircraft
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's corner map now plots the other aircraft live, amber in the air with altitude and grey on the ground, and a Map button or the M key hides it.

item.title: The Kai Tak terminal, rebuilt to match the chart
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's terminal and apron now follow the Kai Tak chart: a pier at right angles to the runway, eight nose-in stands, lanes D3, D2 and D1, and new taxi routes.

item.title: The Flight Board Clatters
item.description: The Fly Kai Tak flight information board now clatters like a real split-flap board whenever a letter changes, on the home screen and in Plane Spotter, with its own on/off button.

item.title: New: Sun, Moon and Time of Day
item.description: Fly Kai Tak now has a sun and moon placed for Hong Kong in 1998, a 24-hour clock with Dawn, Day, Dusk and Night presets, and lighting that follows the sun.

item.title: The Kai Tak Flight Information Board
item.description: Fly Kai Tak adds a split-flap flight information board with every arrival and departure, on the home screen and in Plane Spotter, in English and Cantonese.

item.title: Zoom With the Mouse Wheel
item.description: Fly Kai Tak now zooms with the mouse wheel: scroll up to zoom in, scroll down to zoom out, 1× to 16×, one step per notch.

item.title: Fix: Buildings and Vehicles Clear of Aircraft
item.description: Fly Kai Tak apron fix: aircraft no longer overlap the car park, the fire station or service vehicles, which now wait out of sight until their aircraft docks.

item.title: Home Screen Shows Your Day, Night and Weather Choices
item.description: On the Fly Kai Tak home screen, the live view of Kowloon behind the menu now updates straight away when you toggle day or night, weather, clouds and lightning.

item.title: New: Aircraft Collisions and Damage
item.description: Fly Kai Tak aircraft now have collision detection: ground traffic avoids each other, and a collision shows broken wings, scorch marks, smoke and fire.

item.title: New: jet bridges and pushback tugs at the Kai Tak terminal
item.description: Fly Kai Tak adds jet bridges to the Kai Tak terminal. Aircraft taxi in and dock at them, and pushback tugs push each departure back and turn it toward the runway.

item.title: Apron taxi lines and numbered stands
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's apron now has yellow taxi lines, numbered stands, red stand boxes and service road lines, and the other aircraft taxi along them.

item.title: Blog categories, search and pages
item.description: The Fly Kai Tak blog now has categories, a sort by category view, 20 posts per page and a search box that works in English and Cantonese.

item.title: Fix: the 747 upper-deck hump now has the right shape
item.description: The 747-400 upper-deck hump in Fly Kai Tak was too tall and narrow. It is now lower and wider with a long shallow slope into the roof, like the real 747.

item.title: New: Plane Spotter on Runway 31
item.description: Fly Kai Tak Plane Spotter now has a Runway 31 mode: arrivals over Lei Yue Mun, departures toward Kowloon City, and a Lei Yue Mun spectator view.

item.title: New: take off from Runway 31 in free flight
item.description: Fly Kai Tak free flight now starts on Runway 31 as well as Runway 13, with Runway 31 radio calls, mirrored airport traffic and a climb out over Kowloon City.

item.title: New: a take-off lesson for first-time pilots
item.description: Fly Kai Tak now has a Take-off lesson: a coach panel walks first-time pilots through a Runway 13 take-off in eight steps with live meters and plain-language tips.

item.title: Fix: no more false "too low" calls after take-off
item.description: Fly Kai Tak fix: the "Too low, gear" and "Too low, flaps" warnings no longer fire on take-off. They need a descent now; the IGS 13 approach is unchanged.

item.title: New: ground vehicles on the Kai Tak apron
item.description: Fly Kai Tak adds airport ground vehicles: buses, catering trucks that lift to the door, baggage tractors with loaded carts, container and box freight trucks, and fire tenders at a fire station.

item.title: New: easterly approach to Runway 31
item.description: Fly Kai Tak adds a Runway 31 approach: a straight-in final over the sea, through the Lei Yue Mun gap and across Kowloon Bay, with its own lights, PAPI, radio calls, traffic and spotter view.

item.title: Update: a High scores button on the home screen
item.description: Fly Kai Tak update: a High scores button on the home screen opens and closes the table of ranked landings, from Captain down to Cadet.

item.title: New: share your score and report card
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's result screen now has share buttons for X, Facebook, Reddit, WhatsApp, Threads and email, plus a downloadable report card image.

item.title: New: a high score table with Captain and First Officer ranks
item.description: Fly Kai Tak now has a high score table. Land the IGS 13 approach by hand to rank as Captain, First Officer, Second Officer, Flight Engineer or Cadet.

item.title: New: giant billboards and neon over Kowloon
item.description: Fly Kai Tak now has 1990s-style giant floodlit billboards on Kowloon rooftops and roadsides, plus glowing neon signs. Brands are invented; no real logos.

item.title: Plane spotter viewpoints: the car park roof and the Peak
item.description: The history of two Kai Tak plane spotting viewpoints, the airport car park roof and the Peak, and how to watch from both in Fly Kai Tak's Plane Spotter mode.

item.title: Update: the rotate prompt is gone
item.description: Fly Kai Tak mobile update: the Turn your phone sideways prompt is removed, so the sim plays in either orientation. Begin descent still asks for landscape full screen.

item.title: Fix: the rotate prompt now clears when you turn your phone
item.description: Fly Kai Tak mobile fix: the rotate prompt now clears when the window turns landscape, with a hint for iPhone players whose Portrait Orientation Lock is on.

item.title: Redrawn aircraft: embedded cockpits and real winglets
item.description: Fly Kai Tak update: the 747-400, 777-200, A330-300 and A340-300 are redrawn with embedded cockpit glass, swept winglets and tapered wings.

item.title: Aircraft now turn smoothly on the ground
item.description: Fly Kai Tak fix: other aircraft snapped to a new heading at every taxi corner. They now curve through turns, ease their speed and line up on the runway.

item.title: The airlines and aircraft of Kai Tak
item.description: A guide to the airlines and aircraft types at Kai Tak in the 1990s: Cathay Pacific, Dragonair, Qantas, BA, Singapore, Thai and JAL, with brief histories.

item.title: Other aircraft now bank the right way
item.description: Fly Kai Tak fix: other aircraft were drawn banking the wrong way in turns. Arrivals and departures now dip the inside wing, as real jets do.

item.title: Read the Fly Kai Tak blog in Cantonese
item.description: The Fly Kai Tak blog now has an English / Cantonese toggle on every page: posts, captions, header and footer switch to written Cantonese.

item.title: Fly Kai Tak in Cantonese: a language toggle on the home screen
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's home screen now has an English / Cantonese toggle: the whole setup screen switches to written Cantonese and remembers your choice.

item.title: The Peak Tram, the Peak Lookout and a view from the Peak
item.description: Fly Kai Tak adds the Peak Tram, the Peak Lookout and a Spectator: The Peak view, alongside Ocean Park's cable car between the Waterfront and the Summit.

item.title: An inverted yoke for touch and mouse: drag down to pull up
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's on-screen yoke is now inverted for touch and mouse: drag down to pull the nose up, drag up to push it down, matching the keyboard.

item.title: Share Fly Kai Tak posts on Threads
item.description: Fly Kai Tak blog posts can now be shared on Threads with one click, with the title and link pre-filled.

item.title: Landmarks tour, plus Ocean Park and Happy Valley
item.description: A tour of the Hong Kong landmarks in Fly Kai Tak, with screenshots, plus the new Ocean Park amusement park and Happy Valley Racecourse.

item.title: Flying Kai Tak on your phone: landscape, a cleaner toolbar and bigger controls
item.description: Fly Kai Tak on mobile: a compact toolbar with a More drawer, landscape touch controls, a rotate prompt for portrait, full screen on Begin descent and safe-area support.

item.title: The checkerboard turn: flying the IGS 13 approach
item.description: How the famous Runway 13 IGS approach into Kai Tak works in Fly Kai Tak: the 088° course, the checkerboard on the hill, the 47° right turn over Kowloon City and the landing grade.

item.title: Real Hong Kong: building 1998 from open data
item.description: How Fly Kai Tak builds Hong Kong from Lands Department open data and SRTM terrain, and the 1998 corrections: no Kai Tak redevelopment, no West Kowloon buildings, and the Walled City as an option.

item.title: Typhoons, fog and city lights: weather and night at Kai Tak
item.description: Weather and night flying in Fly Kai Tak: clear, rain, typhoon, storm, low cloud and fog presets, wind gusts and turbulence, lightning, and a lit-up Kowloon at night.
